Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) Stock Value Rose While Montag & Caldwell Cut by $10.93 Million Its Stake; Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company Has Trimmed Its New Residental Investment (NRZ) Stake by $510,000 
April 24, 2018 - By Richard Conner 
Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company decreased its stake in New Residental Investment (NRZ) by 4.75% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company sold 30,000 shares as the company’s stock declined 8.26% with the market. The institutional investor held 602,000 shares of the real estate investment trusts company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $10.77M, down from 632,000 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company who had been investing in New Residental Investment for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $5.57B market cap company. The stock increased 0.21% or $0.03 during the last trading session, reaching $16.58. About 1.28M shares traded. New Residential Investment Corp. (NYSE:NRZ) has risen 0.90% since April 24, 2017 and is uptrending. It has underperformed by 10.65% the S&P500. 
Montag & Caldwell Llc decreased its stake in Intercontinental Exchange Inc (ICE) by 9.67% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Montag & Caldwell Llc sold 156,129 shares as the company’s stock rose 2.21% while stock markets declined. The institutional investor held 1.46 million shares of the investment bankers and brokers and service company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $102.96M, down from 1.62 million at the end of the previous reported quarter. (NYSE:ICE) has risen 20.88% since April 24, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 9.33% the S&P500.

ICE’s profit will be $511.26 million for 20.71 P/E if the $0.88 EPS becomes a reality.
